    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md",
    "text": "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
    to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative state for the purpose
    of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative state has sufficient staffing,
    expertise, and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative
    state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant
    pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement through
    the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal
    written notice of the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty
    (30) days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall
    set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
    An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section
    \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice
    of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
    requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing:
    \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
    meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
    a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires
    control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control
    of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator,
    or trustee, or as an officer appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction
    or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)];
    \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section
    6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities
    of a licensee or a person in control of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization
    of a person in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control
    of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3),
    (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner]
    within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
    procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived from other \naspects
    of state law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect the relevant
    administrative process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied upon updating the
    licensee’s NMLS record.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
    An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section
    \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice
    of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe
    requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing:
    \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated
    meeting of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
    a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person that acquires
    control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA person that acquires control
    of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative, custodian, guardian, conservator,

    or by operation of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)];

    "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000024",
    "start": 0, "end": 2799, "page_number": 24, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md",
    "text": "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements
    of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied with
    and received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this [Act] or was
    identified as a person in control in a prior application filed with and \napproved
    by the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing
    process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended
    or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked or suspended while the
    person \nwas in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the
    person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas received at least a
    satisfactory rating for compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB
    accredited state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired
    is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]
    of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed, and if the person
    acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee is also projected to meet the
    requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition
    of control is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement
    any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of
    control, and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee also
    will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of
    the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition
    in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B),
    (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2)
    \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date on \nwhich the
    notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore
    filing an application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson
    may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner] as to whether the
    person \nwould be considered a person in control of a licensee upon consummation
    of a proposed \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person
    would not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction
    is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act].
    \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes a determination pursuant to
    \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to
    the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state
    with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of
    [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    "source_hash": "4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680",

    "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe requirements of
    [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson that has complied with and
    received approval to engage in money transmission \nunder this [Act] or was identified
    as a person in control in a prior application filed with and \napproved by the
    [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing
    process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or suspended

    person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas received at least a

    accredited state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired
    is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]

    any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of
    control, and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee also
    will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of
    the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition
    in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B),
    (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2)
    \nIf the notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date on \nwhich the
    notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore
    filing an application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a \nperson
    may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner] as to whether the
    person \nwould be considered a person in control of a licensee upon consummation
    of a proposed \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person
    would not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction
    is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)] of this [Act].
    \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes a determination pursuant to
    \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to
    the multistate licensing \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and
    encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state
    with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the purpose of
    [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538", "source_version":
    "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization
    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000004",
    "start": 298, "end": 2509, "page_number": 4, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "2245b178c49fc1f157bf15c133c59f8fcfe9abdf43f0bf94df397229a7889584", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000004.md",
    "text": "ly for goods or services provided by the issuer or its affiliate or franchisees
    of the issuer \nor its affiliate, except to the extent required by applicable
    law to be redeemable in cash for its cash \nvalue; \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1)
    \n(A) the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe
    outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person in control
    of a \nlicensee; \n(B) \nthe power to elect or appoint a majority of key individuals
    or \nexecutive officers, managers, directors, trustees, or other persons exercising
    \nmanagerial authority of a person in control of a licensee; or \n(C) \nthe power
    to exercise, directly or indirectly, a controlling \ninfluence over the management
    or policies of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable
    Presumption of Control. \n(A) \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling
    influence \nwhen the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at
    least 10 percent \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee
    or person in control \nof a licensee.2 \n(B) \nA person presumed to exercise a
    controlling influence as \ndefined by this [Section 2.01(f)] can rebut the presumption
    of control if the person \nis a passive investor. \n(3) \nFor purposes of determining
    the percentage of a person controlled \nby any other person, the person''s interest
    shall be aggregated with the interest of any other \nimmediate family member,
    including the person''s spouse, parents, children, siblings, \nmothers- and fathers-in
    law, sons- and daughters-in-law, brothers- and sisters-in-law, and \nany other
    person who shares such person''s home. \n(g) \n\"Eligible rating\" shall mean
    a credit rating of any of the three highest rating \ncategories provided by an
    eligible rating service, whereby each category may include rating \n \n2 Commentary:
    The obligation to rebut control rests exclusively with the person acquiring ≥10%
    of the outstanding \nvoting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person
    in control of a licensee.  It is not the responsibility of the \nlicensee to rebut
    control.  This is consistent with Section 601(a) of the Act which requires the

    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000004.md",
    "source_hash": "2245b178c49fc1f157bf15c133c59f8fcfe9abdf43f0bf94df397229a7889584",
    "source_label": "[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 4, characters
    298–2509", "unit_id": "p000004", "locator": "Page 4, characters 298–2509", "available_excerpt":
    "ly for goods or services provided by the issuer or its affiliate or franchisees
    of the issuer \nor its affiliate, except to the extent required by applicable
    law to be redeemable in cash for its cash \nvalue; \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1)
    \n(A) the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe
    outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person in control
    of a \nlicensee; \n(B) \nthe power to elect or appoint a majority of key individuals
    or \nexecutive officers, managers, directors, trustees, or other persons exercising
    \nmanagerial authority of a person in control of a licensee; or \n(C) \nthe power
    to exercise, directly or indirectly, a controlling \ninfluence over the management
    or policies of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable
    Presumption of Control. \n(A) \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling
    influence \nwhen the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at
    least 10 percent \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee
    or person in control \nof a licensee.2 \n(B) \nA person presumed to exercise a
    controlling influence as \ndefined by this [Section 2.01(f)] can rebut the presumption
    of control if the person \nis a passive investor. \n(3) \nFor purposes of determining
    the percentage of a person controlled \nby any other person, the person''s interest
    shall be aggregated with the interest of any other \nimmediate family member,
    including the person''s spouse, parents, children, siblings, \nmothers- and fathers-in
    law, sons- and daughters-in-law, brothers- and sisters-in-law, and \nany other
    person who shares such person''s home. \n(g) \n\"Eligible rating\" shall mean
    a credit rating of any of the three highest rating \ncategories provided by an
    eligible rating service, whereby each category may include rating \n \n2 Commentary:
    The obligation to rebut control rests exclusively with the person acquiring ≥10%
    of the outstanding \nvoting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person
    in control of a licensee.  It is not the responsibility of the \nlicensee to rebut
    control.  This is consistent with Section 601(a) of the Act which requires the
    person acquiring control \nto obtain prior approval.\n"}, {"source_id": "SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538",

    [{"unit_id": "p000030", "start": 0, "end": 2670, "page_number": 30, "section_label":

    "text": "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the licensee''s
    authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money transmission on behalf
    of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature and scope of the relationship between
    the \nlicensee and the authorized delegate and the respective rights and responsibilities
    of the \nparties; \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate to agree to fully comply
    with all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules, and regulations pertaining
    to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act] and regulations implementing this
    [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT;
    \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate to remit and handle money and \nmonetary
    value in accordance with the terms of the contract between the licensee and the
    \nauthorized delegate; \n(5) \nimpose a trust on money and monetary value net
    of fees received for \nmoney transmission for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6)
    \nrequire the authorized delegate to prepare and maintain records as \nrequired
    by this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act], or as reasonably requested
    \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge that the authorized delegate consents
    to examination \nor investigation by the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the
    licensee is subject to regulation by the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of
    that regulation, the [Commissioner] may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized delegate
    designation or require the licensee to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation;
    and \n(9) \n(9)  acknowledge receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired
    under [Section 8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee''s license is suspended, revoked,
    surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5) business days, provide
    documentation to the [Commissioner] that \nthe licensee has notified all applicable
    authorized delegates of the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord filed with
    the [Commissioner] of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of
    a \nlicense. Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license,
    applicable authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide money transmission
    as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f) \nAn authorized delegate of
    a licensee holds in trust for the benefit of the \nlicensee all money net of fees
    received from money transmission.  If any authorized delegate \ncommingles any
    funds received from money transmission with any other funds or property owned
    \nor controlled by the authorized delegate, all commingled funds and other property
    shall be \nconsidered held in trust in favor of the licensee in an amount equal
    to the amount of money net of\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "p000031",
    "start": 0, "end": 2704, "page_number": 31, "section_label": null, "body_hash":
    "994d5382d8c2640923eca8c8aabbca98c8fbaeec037edafbf7675c1a3819b1e7", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000031.md",
    "text": "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
    delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission on behalf of
    a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA person shall not engage
    in the business of money transmission on behalf of a person \nnot licensed under
    this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant to [Article III] of this [Act]. A person that
    \nengages in such activity provides money transmission to the same extent as if
    the person were a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally liable with the
    unlicensed or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized
    Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by a licensee
    shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable or legal relief, including
    without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized delegate from directly or indirectly
    acting as an authorized delegate for any licensee \nin this state and the payment
    of restitution, damages or other monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt]
    finds that an authorized delegate failed to remit money in accordance with the
    written \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed by the
    licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court] issues an order
    prohibiting a person from acting as \nan authorized delegate for any licensee
    pursuant to [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee that brought the \naction shall report
    the order to the [Commissioner] within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder
    through NMLS within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds
    money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit more
    than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification]
    felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust for the benefit
    of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money
    is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely
    Transmission, Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a)
    \nEvery licensee shall forward all money received for transmission in \naccordance
    with the terms of the agreement between the licensee and the sender unless the
    licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a reasonable basis to believe that the sender
    may be a victim of fraud or \nthat a crime or violation of law, rule, or regulation
    has occurred, is occurring, or may occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward
    money received for transmission in accordance \nwith this section, the licensee
    must respond to inquiries by the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22
    Commentary: An express trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"}],

    An express trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"}, {"source_id":
    "SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4", "source_version": "d021ece0cde82565eb83511c8122c85b",
    "title": "Money Transmitter Licensing | Department of Financial Services", "extraction_state":
    "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "s000001", "start": 2400, "end":
    7324, "page_number": null, "section_label": "Section 1", "body_hash": "3c6e0983ad889dc93334add58721659be3ac3d4bf1075f544bcd9c940396e471",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4/d021ece0cde82565eb83511c8122c85b/sections/s000001.md",
    "text": "ey Transmitter License.\n\nAccess to NMLS\n\nNMLS is a secure web-based
    system created by state regulators to provide efficiencies in the processing of
    state licenses and improve supervision of state-regulated industries.\n\nTo access
    NMLS for the first time, you must complete a Company Account Request Form and
    identify a Primary Account Administrator and a Secondary Account Administrator.
    This form can be submitted online through the NMLS website in the Getting Started
    section. This form needs to be submitted only once per company, regardless of
    the number of NMLS participating states in which you are licensed.\n\nWithin three
    days of completing and submitting the Company Account Request Form, the Primary
    Account Administrator will receive NMLS login information. The Primary Account
    Administrator will have full rights to access the system, submit information to
    this agency and other participating state regulators, and set up other company
    users in the system. Instructions and tutorials on how to access and use the system
    are also available in the NMLS Resource Center .\n\nNote : If your company already
    has a record in NMLS, you can omit this step.\n\nManaging Your License on NMLS\n\nEach
    company holding a DFS Money Transmitter License who wishes to manage their license
    on NMLS must create a company record in the system. To gain access to NMLS, the
    applicant must submit a form requesting an NMLS account.\n\nCurrent New York State
    Money Transmitters may transition their licenses to NMLS. See the DFS Money Transmitter
    Transition Checklist for more information.\n\nSubmitting a Complete Application\n\nTo
    submit an application and ensure your application is received, acknowledged as
    complete, and processed, please follow the instructions on the DFS Money Transmitter
    Checklists . No application shall be deemed to be complete until the Department
    has received all required information, documents, and fees.\n\nIn the process
    of reviewing and considering the application, DFS may request additional information
    and supporting documents.\n\nIn the application process, an NMLS Identification
    Number will be assigned to your application. Please maintain a record of this
    NMLS Identification Number, as it will be used as your application reference number
    throughout the remainder of the application process. The applicant’s NMLS Identification
    Number must be included on every hard-copy document submitted to the Department.\n\nNote
    : If the applicant has already submitted Forms MU1 and MU2 through NMLS for another
    state, the applicant does not need to re-enter the company record into NMLS. However,
    the applicant is required to provide jurisdiction-specific information to support
    its New York State application.\n\nBack to Top ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nAnnual
    Reporting\n\nThe Annual Report should be prepared by qualified persons and submitted
    within 120 days following the close of the calendar year January 1 to December
    31, 2025.\n\n2025 NMLS Money Transmitter Annual Report Form\n\n2025 Non-NMLS Money
    Transmitter Annual Report Form\n\nBack to Top ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nReporting
    Change in Certain Individuals\n\nPursuant to the following sections of the New
    York Banking Law (BL) and Superintendent’s Regulations (SR), licensees of the
    Department of Financial Services (DFS) are required to notify the Superintendent
    of changes in certain individuals, within stipulated time frames:\n\nMoney Transmitters:
    BL 641, 642 and 652-a; and SR 406.11\n\nThese requirements are for changes in
    certain individuals of licensees whose licenses are not managed on NMLS. For those
    managed on NMLS, visit the NMLS section website for New York State and navigate
    to Company Licenses and Amendment under the pertinent industry type, and look
    under Change in Control on the Amendment Checklist.\n\nIncluded Individuals\n\nMembers
    of the governing board such as directors, trustees, and LLC members\n\nOfficers
    (at a minimum Chief Executive Officer, President, Chief Financial Officer, Chief
    Compliance Officer, and Chief Operations Officer, and any other officers deemed
    necessary by DFS)\n\nDocumentary requirements for Each Included Individual Being
    Added\n\nNotification on the licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized officer
    containing the following:\n\nName and title of the individual being added\n\nEffective
    date of the addition\n\nName and title of the person being replaced, and his/her
    new title/position, if any\n\nResolution of the governing board approving the
    addition\n\nPersonal Questionnaire (PDF)\n\nFingerprints\n\nBackground Investigation
    Report *\n\nLitigation Affidavit (PDF)\n\nAuthority to Release Information (PDF)\n\nResume\n\nDocumentary
    requirements for Each Included Individual Being Removed:\n\nNotification on the
    licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized officer containing the following:\n\nName
    and title of the individual being removed\n\nReason of the removal\n\nEffective
    date of the removal\n\nNew title/position, if any\n\nWhere To Submit?"}], "support_state":
    "retrieved", "url": "https://www.dfs.ny.gov/apps_and_licensing/money_transmitters",
    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/RUN-20260911-d08e84-71b20ecf65825d6522c4-fetch.md.bin",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4/d021ece0cde82565eb83511c8122c85b/sections/s000001.md",
    "source_hash": "3c6e0983ad889dc93334add58721659be3ac3d4bf1075f544bcd9c940396e471",
    "source_label": "Money Transmitter Licensing | Department of Financial Services
    — Section 1, characters 2400–7324", "unit_id": "s000001", "locator": "Section
    1, characters 2400–7324", "available_excerpt": "ey Transmitter License.\n\nAccess
    to NMLS\n\nNMLS is a secure web-based system created by state regulators to provide
    efficiencies in the processing of state licenses and improve supervision of state-regulated
    industries.\n\nTo access NMLS for the first time, you must complete a Company
    Account Request Form and identify a Primary Account Administrator and a Secondary
    Account Administrator. This form can be submitted online through the NMLS website
    in the Getting Started section. This form needs to be submitted only once per
    company, regardless of the number of NMLS participating states in which you are
    licensed.\n\nWithin three days of completing and submitting the Company Account
    Request Form, the Primary Account Administrator will receive NMLS login information.
    The Primary Account Administrator will have full rights to access the system,
    submit information to this agency and other participating state regulators, and
    set up other company users in the system. Instructions and tutorials on how to
    access and use the system are also available in the NMLS Resource Center .\n\nNote
    : If your company already has a record in NMLS, you can omit this step.\n\nManaging
    Your License on NMLS\n\nEach company holding a DFS Money Transmitter License who
    wishes to manage their license on NMLS must create a company record in the system.
    To gain access to NMLS, the applicant must submit a form requesting an NMLS account.\n\nCurrent
    New York State Money Transmitters may transition their licenses to NMLS. See the
    DFS Money Transmitter Transition Checklist for more information.\n\nSubmitting
    a Complete Application\n\nTo submit an application and ensure your application
    is received, acknowledged as complete, and processed, please follow the instructions
    on the DFS Money Transmitter Checklists . No application shall be deemed to be
    complete until the Department has received all required information, documents,
    and fees.\n\nIn the process of reviewing and considering the application, DFS
    may request additional information and supporting documents.\n\nIn the application
    process, an NMLS Identification Number will be assigned to your application. Please
    maintain a record of this NMLS Identification Number, as it will be used as your
    application reference number throughout the remainder of the application process.
    The applicant’s NMLS Identification Number must be included on every hard-copy
    document submitted to the Department.\n\nNote : If the applicant has already submitted
    Forms MU1 and MU2 through NMLS for another state, the applicant does not need
    to re-enter the company record into NMLS. However, the applicant is required to
    provide jurisdiction-specific information to support its New York State application.\n\nBack
    to Top ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nAnnual Reporting\n\nThe Annual Report
    should be prepared by qualified persons and submitted within 120 days following
    the close of the calendar year January 1 to December 31, 2025.\n\n2025 NMLS Money
    Transmitter Annual Report Form\n\n2025 Non-NMLS Money Transmitter Annual Report
    Form\n\nBack to Top ▲\n\nNext Section\n\nContinue\n\nReporting Change in Certain
    Individuals\n\nPursuant to the following sections of the New York Banking Law
    (BL) and Superintendent’s Regulations (SR), licensees of the Department of Financial
    Services (DFS) are required to notify the Superintendent of changes in certain
    individuals, within stipulated time frames:\n\nMoney Transmitters: BL 641, 642
    and 652-a; and SR 406.11\n\nThese requirements are for changes in certain individuals
    of licensees whose licenses are not managed on NMLS. For those managed on NMLS,
    visit the NMLS section website for New York State and navigate to Company Licenses
    and Amendment under the pertinent industry type, and look under Change in Control
    on the Amendment Checklist.\n\nIncluded Individuals\n\nMembers of the governing
    board such as directors, trustees, and LLC members\n\nOfficers (at a minimum Chief
    Executive Officer, President, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Compliance Officer,
    and Chief Operations Officer, and any other officers deemed necessary by DFS)\n\nDocumentary
    requirements for Each Included Individual Being Added\n\nNotification on the licensee''s
    letterhead signed by an authorized officer containing the following:\n\nName and
    title of the individual being added\n\nEffective date of the addition\n\nName
    and title of the person being replaced, and his/her new title/position, if any\n\nResolution
    of the governing board approving the addition\n\nPersonal Questionnaire (PDF)\n\nFingerprints\n\nBackground
    Investigation Report *\n\nLitigation Affidavit (PDF)\n\nAuthority to Release Information
    (PDF)\n\nResume\n\nDocumentary requirements for Each Included Individual Being
    Removed:\n\nNotification on the licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized
    officer containing the following:\n\nName and title of the individual being removed\n\nReason
    of the removal\n\nEffective date of the removal\n\nNew title/position, if any\n\nWhere
    To Submit?"}, {"source_id": "SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200", "source_version": "6ebc7b743e605b8e05363eb0628942c1",
    "title": "How To Get A Money Transmitter License (MTL) in the U.S. - Fenergo",
    "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "s000002", "start":
    0, "end": 3321, "page_number": null, "section_label": "Section 2", "body_hash":
    "b8cfb71cc698f4b53cce08d023441fce54bf275adbcb1164dfb05a05143f6ba9", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200/6ebc7b743e605b8e05363eb0628942c1/sections/s000002.md",
    "text": "How To Get A Money Transmitter License (MTL) in the U.S.\n\nPublished
    Date  January 29, 2026\n\nTo get a Money Transmitter License (MTL), businesses
    must undergo a rigorous application process that involves dual compliance with
    federal (like FinCEN''s AML/KYC protocols) and varying state-level regulations.
    Key requirements across states include demonstrating financial viability, often
    requiring a surety bond and capital reserves, passing comprehensive background
    checks for key personnel, and establishing a robust internal compliance program.
    The process is complex, time-consuming, and mandates extensive documentation and
    financial disclosures to ensure the applicant is law-abiding and financially sound.\n\nOperating
    a money transfer service in the U.S. involves tackling a myriad of federal and
    state laws, making how to get a money transmitter license both time-consuming
    and expensive. Compliance with agencies like FinCEN is non-negotiable to prevent
    illegal activities.\n\nCompanies can either secure their own MSB license or partner
    with a licensed entity, but legal adherence is vital in both scenarios. It''s
    essential to understand what a money transmitter license is and who needs it.\n\nWhat
    is a Money Transmitter License?\n\nA Money Transmitter License is an official
    authorization or money service business license that empowers a firm or individual
    to facilitate the movement of capital. This license enables MSBs to handle financial
    transactions, ranging from digital payments to wire transfers.\n\nPossessing a
    Money Transmitter License brings forth substantial regulatory oversight. Organizations
    must prove they have the governance structure and internal controls to manage
    and safeguard client funds. States will continually scrutinize applicants, denying
    licensure to those who fail to meet the stringent criteria.\n\nIn the United States,
    the need for a Money Transmitter License is not a choice; it''s a requirement
    for virtually any business involved in the handling or transferring of funds.
    Money transmitter license requirements by state can vary, so it''s crucial to
    be aware of the respective state money transmitter regulations.\n\nHow to Get
    a Money Transmitter License?\n\nThe license application process is designed to
    be rigorous, ensuring that approved businesses are law-abiding and financially
    sound. Federal and state-level regulations diverge, with each state setting its
    own financial criteria and often requiring a minimum capital commitment.\n\nApplicants
    typically need a surety bond of at least $500,000 per state, with costs influenced
    by credit history. The duration to obtain the license varies, contingent on the
    business type and the state of operation.\n\nMoney Transmitter License Requirements\n\nAcquiring
    a money transmitter license involves compliance with Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
    and Know Your Customer (KYC) protocols. While these regulations are federal, individual
    states often impose additional requirements, thereby necessitating dual compliance.\n\nSubsequent
    to application submission, state authorities undertake an investigative review,
    focusing on financial sustainability and the applicant''s background.\n\nStandardized
    Requirements Across States\n\nRegistration: Initial registration typically occurs
    with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network or a similar state-level body."}],

    {"source_id": "SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413", "source_version": "e06621859d4ec9431f2712a7c357b112",
    "title": "OCC Confirms National Bank Act Preempts State Money Transmitter ...",
    "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages": [{"unit_id": "s000001", "start":
    600, "end": 4794, "page_number": null, "section_label": "Section 1", "body_hash":
    "8ef30c0b98621db1f11c16332c16e9928ea8f237d6b055f645f7b449f18cbdfb", "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413/e06621859d4ec9431f2712a7c357b112/sections/s000001.md",
    "text": ", 2026\n\nPosted in Bank Regulatory\n\nOn May 12, the Office of the Comptroller
    of the Currency (OCC) issued a significant interpretive letter confirming that
    Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association (the recently converted national
    trust bank formerly known as Fidelity Digital Assets Service, LLC) is not required
    to hold state money transmitter licenses to conduct its federally authorized activities.
    The OCC concluded that the National Bank Act preempts any state money transmitter
    licensing requirement as applied to a national bank.\n\nUntil December 12, 2025,
    Fidelity Digital Assets operated as a New York-chartered limited liability trust
    company and held money transmitter licenses in numerous states, including Iowa.
    On that date, the OCC approved its conversion to an uninsured national trust bank
    under 12 U.S.C. § 27(a). Concurrent with the conversion, the Bank surrendered
    its Iowa money transmitter license.\n\nIowa pushed back. Its money transmitter
    statute exempts banks and trust companies from licensing, but only if they hold
    federally insured deposits. Because Fidelity Digital Assets is an uninsured national
    bank, Iowa argued the exemption did not apply and requested a legal basis for
    the license surrender. Fidelity Digital Assets responded that the National Bank
    Act preempts Iowa’s requirements and asked the OCC to confirm that position.\n\nThe
    OCC’s analysis of whether a state can require a national bank to obtain a state
    money transmitter license as a condition of engaging in federally authorized activities,
    including cryptocurrency custody, trade execution, stablecoin issuance, and related
    digital asset services, rested on two independent and well-established pillars
    of federal banking law:\n\n1. National Bank Act Preemption\n\nFederal law authorizes
    national banks to conduct a broad range of activities on a national basis. Any
    state law that “prevents or significantly interferes” with a national bank’s exercise
    of its federally authorized powers is preempted.\n\nThe OCC reasoned that requiring
    a national bank to obtain a state money transmitter license, even as a threshold
    condition to operating, would impermissibly condition the Bank’s federal authority
    on state approval. At the extreme, a state could veto federal authority outright
    by denying or revoking a license. Both outcomes are squarely preempted. This conclusion
    applies to any state’s money transmitter licensing regime, including states that
    limit their licensing exemptions to a subset of national banks (such as Iowa’s
    insured-deposits-only carveout).\n\n2. Exclusive Federal Visitorial Authority\n\nSeparately,
    12 U.S.C. § 484 vests the OCC with exclusive visitorial authority over national
    banks. “No national bank shall be subject to any visitorial powers except as authorized
    by Federal law.” Iowa’s money transmitter statute grants the state agency robust
    supervisory jurisdiction over licensees, including the power to demand books and
    records, conduct periodic examinations, take enforcement actions, and even place
    a licensee into receivership. Applying that regime to a national bank would be
    “fundamentally inconsistent” with the OCC’s exclusive visitorial powers and is
    therefore impermissible on independent grounds.\n\nTogether, these two bases lead
    to a clean and sweeping conclusion: a national bank may conduct its federally
    authorized activities in any state without a state money transmitter license,
    regardless of whether it qualifies for any state-law exemption.\n\nOur Take\n\nThe
    OCC’s conclusion here was entirely expected. The preemption framework for national
    banks is well-settled, and the OCC’s letter largely restates principles the Supreme
    Court and federal courts have applied for decades. That said, one nuance in this
    letter deserves closer attention: state-chartered trust banks are in a very different
    position.\n\nUnlike national banks, state trust companies and state-chartered
    banks do not benefit from National Bank Act preemption. Their ability to avoid
    state money transmitter licensing requirements depends entirely on how each individual
    state defines “bank” or “trust company” in its money transmission statute and
    those definitions vary considerably.\n\nPrint:"}], "support_state": "retrieved",

    "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
    Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n-
    Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s
    app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
    to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n-
    Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
    results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
    2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
    first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a
    handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration
    moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
    day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
    of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC
    ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone
    but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
    transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
    plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
    — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
    or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
    What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year?
    — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened
    by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
    licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023
    Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic
    Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
    It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on
    Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and
    the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
    — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what is the
    plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those
    customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses
    for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s

    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring

    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure

    "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
    (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
    and full access to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor
    users were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
    (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
    four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
    Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for
    users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party
    SaaS whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with
    a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
    alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
    them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
    Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n-
    Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
    before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay
    acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does
    Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s
    prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
    / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts
    and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
    to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume
    Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
    and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have
    the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
    and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed
    and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined license
    footprint, what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
    Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
    or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML

    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n"}], "content_truncated": false, "source_label": "facts.md"},

    "source_version": "e4242fa79f3b92949785891f5244f2974e8cd7f13b04fe492c2bfec99c9f576f",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-843f945d0832ba97e71a.md",
    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/dossier.md", "title": "dossier.md",
    "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
    "# Harbor 2 matter dossier\n\n## Current position\n\nThe Harbor Pay migration
    needs legal and compliance review before the planned Nov 15 close. This is the
    accepted working view. No decision has been recorded.\n\nThis draft recommends
    continuing close preparation but making the day-one service migration conditional.
    Mosaic should not give all Harbor users full access until:\n\n1. Mosaic has documented
    authority for each post-close service in each affected state.\n2. Compliance confirms
    that Mosaic may rely on Harbor’s know-your-customer (KYC) results, or defines
    and completes remediation.\n3. Authorized reviewers assess Harbor’s open alerts
    and suspicious activity report (SAR) history.\n4. Mosaic tests the replacement
    transaction-monitoring feed and finds no material coverage gap.\n\nIf a condition
    is not met, Mosaic should hold the affected state launch, restrict affected accounts,
    or delay full product access. The $50 welcome bonus should also wait for review
    of its structure, terms, funding, and disclosures.\n\nThe saved material does
    not establish that the acquisition close itself must wait. However, the unread
    alerts and SAR history could affect deal terms, risk allocation, or the decision
    to close.\n\n### Assumptions used\n\n- Harbor is subject to the state money-transmission
    and federal anti-money-laundering requirements discussed below. The licensing,
    KYC, alert, and monitoring conclusions depend on this unverified legal premise.\n-
    Mosaic will become the operating provider when Harbor users receive a unified
    Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products. The licensing
    analysis depends on this inference.\n- The analysis does not assume that Harbor’s
    licenses transfer, that Harbor’s KYC results satisfy Mosaic’s program, or that
    the monitoring transition will work without a gap.\n\n### Record conflicts\n\n-
    Harbor reportedly has licenses in 38 states, Mosaic has licenses in 41 states,
    and the combined footprint is 44 states. A 44-state footprint is three states
    larger than Mosaic’s 41-state footprint, but the record says the acquisition opens
    four new markets. The license lists and the intended meaning of “market” are needed.
    Until then, the states requiring separate authority cannot be identified reliably.\n-
    Matter metadata gives a target date of `2026-09-11`. The reported close is “Nov
    15,” approximately ten weeks after the Sept. 9 intake. A saved hypothetical uses
    November 15, 2026, but that does not establish the actual closing year. The operative
    close date and year remain unresolved.\n\n## Decision question\n\nDoes any part
    of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close?\n\n##
    Issues\n\n<!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045 -->\n### Money transmission
    licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined 44-state footprint
    and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n\n**Current answer**\n\nMosaic
    should not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets that automatically
    move to Mosaic through the reported asset purchase. Mosaic should not start regulated
    services in a state unless it has documented authority for its complete post-close
    activity.\n\nThe acquisition close and the service launch can be managed as separate
    milestones. If authority is not established, the present fallback is to hold the
    affected state launch or restrict regulated functions.\n\n**Rule and support**\n\nSaved
    research concludes that the answer must be determined state by state. The review
    must cover Mosaic’s authority, transaction notices or approvals, interim operations,
    outstanding customer obligations, and Harbor’s license surrender.\n\nFour sources
    were retrieved, but no operative passage was selected, read, or verified. They
    do not establish the rule in any affected state:\n\n- [Money transmission research
    packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)\n- [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538]\n-
    [source:SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4]\n- [source:SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413]\n- [source:SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200]\n\nThe
    model act is not proof of any state’s adopted law. The premise that an asset purchase
    does not automatically give Mosaic Harbor’s operating authority remains an unverified
    state-law conclusion.\n\n**Application**\n\nMosaic plans to use or assume Harbor’s
    licenses in the new markets. The planned unified Mosaic account, combined balance,
    and access to Mosaic products indicate that Mosaic may become the actual provider.
    If so, keeping Harbor’s entity or licenses active might not authorize Mosaic’s
    conduct.\n\nHarbor could remain the licensed provider during a transition only
    if customer contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses, bonds, records,
    and applicable state rules support that result. The documents and actual operations
    must match.\n\nA partner bank holding funds would not alone resolve the issue.
    The analysis still depends on who contracts with users, controls transfers, owes
    repayment, records balances, resolves errors, and performs regulated duties.\n\n**Next
    step**\n\nIdentify the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare a state matrix. For
    each state, determine Mosaic’s authority, required filings or approvals, operation
    while an application is pending, treatment of customer obligations, Harbor’s run-off
    duties, and the launch restriction needed if authority is not established.\n\n<!--
    retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start -->\n<details>\n<summary>Saved
    research and prior analysis</summary>\n\nPreserved research snapshot. Its facts
    and assumptions may predate later records. Use the current answer above for application
    to the current matter.\n\nDo not rely on transferability without an applicable
    state rule, approval, or written regulator position.\n\nThe answer must be determined
    state by state and must cover more than technical change-of-control rules.\n\nThis
    path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider and the relevant states
    permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account design may conflict with that
    position.\n\nT", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 6000, "text": "# Harbor

    the licensee engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file
    a report with the [Commissioner] within three business \nday after the licensee
    has reason to know of the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \na
    [charge or] conviction of the licensee or of a key individual \nor person in control

    delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee
    and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required by federal currency
    \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity reporting requirements as
    set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other federal and state laws pertaining
    to money laundering. The timely filing of \na complete and accurate report required
    under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant
    with the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee

    and bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission

    "text": "4 \n \nJune 30, September 30, and December 31. \n(d) \n\"Bank Secrecy

    goods or services provided by the issuer or its affiliate or franchisees of the
    issuer \nor its affiliate, except to the extent required by applicable law to
    be redeemable in cash for its cash \nvalue; \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1) \n(A)
    the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe outstanding
    voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee;
    \n(B) \nthe power to elect or appoint a majority of key individuals or \nexecutive
    officers, managers, directors, trustees, or other persons exercising \nmanagerial

    directly or indirectly, a controlling \ninfluence over the management or policies
    of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable Presumption
    of Control. \n(A) \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling influence \nwhen
    the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least 10 percent
    \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or person
    in control \nof a licensee.2 \n(B) \nA person presumed to exercise a controlling
    influence as \ndefined by this [Section 2.01(f)] can rebut the presumption of

    "support_state": "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt":
    "# Issues and workstreams\n\n- Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay
    can operate under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
    the acquisition\n- BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with
    missing underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent
    CIP/AML obligations\n- SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and
    manage Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring
    vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract
    terminates at close\n- Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any
    state money transmission or consumer protection implications\n- Customer account,
    contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
    -->\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 817, "text": "# Issues and workstreams\n\n-
    Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under the combined
    44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive the acquisition\n-
    BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing underlying
    documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s independent CIP/AML obligations\n-
    SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage Harbor''s ~40
    open alerts and SARs, and successor liability\n- Monitoring vendor transition:
    continuity of transaction monitoring when the SaaS contract terminates at close\n-
    Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state money transmission
    or consumer protection implications\n- Customer account, contract, and data-transfer
    rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06 -->\n"}], "content_truncated":
    false, "source_label": "issues.md"}, {"source_id": "SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c",

    "original_path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md", "title": "facts.md", "support_state":
    "supplied", "source_type": "workspace", "available_excerpt": "# Known Facts\n\n-
    Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks out).\n-
    Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s
    app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance and full access
    to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.\n-
    Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic has pass/fail
    results for everyone but not the underlying documents for users onboarded before
    2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at Mosaic''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on
    first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a
    handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.\n- Migration
    moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into Mosaic Relay''s app on
    day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n- Plan is no re-verification
    of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC
    ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail results exist for everyone
    but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s
    transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates at close;
    plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.\n-
    Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year
    at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured?
    — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program currently permit relying on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification,
    or is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance\n-
    What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the last year?
    — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n- For the four new markets opened
    by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing
    licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023
    Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic
    Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification and recordkeeping obligations? —
    It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on
    Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have the ~40 open alerts and
    the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
    — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint, what is the
    plan for state money transmission licensing or approval before onboarding those
    customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor''s licenses
    for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s
    existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can
    be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML
    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n", "selected_passages": [{"start": 0, "end": 3962, "text":
    "# Known Facts\n\n- Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
    (~10 weeks out).\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance
    and full access to Mosaic''s product set.\n- Plan is no re-verification; Harbor
    users were already KYC''d by Harbor.\n- Harbor holds money transmitter licenses
    (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
    four new markets.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024;
    Mosaic has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents for
    users onboarded before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party
    SaaS whose contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.\n- Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with
    a $50 bonus on first transfer, launching close+1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open
    alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read
    them yet.\n- Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
    Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and balance.\n-
    Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users were already
    KYC''d.\n- Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for users onboarded
    before 2023.\n- Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
    terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic Relay''s
    engine on day 1.\n- Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.\n- How is the Harbor Pay
    acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)\n- Does
    Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another institution''s
    prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification required? — Not sure
    / need to check with compliance\n- What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts
    and the SARs from the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence\n-
    For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic Relay plan
    to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for its own? — Use/assume
    Harbor''s licenses\n- For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
    and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP
    program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.\n- Have
    the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year been reviewed,
    and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed
    and remain in diligence.\n- For the four new markets opened by the combined license
    footprint, what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume
    Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.\n\n## Assumptions\n\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable
    or can be maintained through the acquisition without new state approval\n- [Assumption]
    The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML
    program obligations without the underlying documents\n- [Assumption] The transaction
    monitoring repoint can be completed and validated before close without a monitoring
    gap\n- [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to state
    MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).\n- [Assumption]
    Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in 41 states (per the request).\n-
    [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase, which
    affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer (structure
    not yet confirmed).\n"}], "content_truncated": false, "source_label": "facts.md"},

    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000027.md",
    "text": "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include or be accompanied
    by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified public accountant or
    independent public \naccountant that is satisfactory in form and content to the
    [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner]
    may order the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
    to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent public
    accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
    \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45
    days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized
    and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report required by
    this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the
    requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall
    include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name;
    \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier;
    \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted
    in other states; \n(7) \nAny fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person
    name, phone number, and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate;
    \n(10) \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;  \n(11)
    \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny other information
    the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect to the authorized delegate.
    \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21 \n \n20 Commentary: This language
    is designed to implement state use of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting
    \n(UAAR) process. \n21 Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy
    Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize
    reporting of significant events.\n"}], "support_state": "retrieved", "url": "https://www.csbs.org/sites/default/files/2023-02/CSBS%20Money%20Transmission%20Modernization%20Act.pdf",

    by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent certified public accountant or

    [Commissioner]. If the certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner]
    may order the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
    to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent public
    accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized Delegate Reporting.
    \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of authorized delegates within 45
    days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20 The [Commissioner] is authorized
    and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS for the submission of the report required by
    this [Section 7.03(a)] provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the
    requirements of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall
    include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate''s: \n(1) \nCompany legal name;
    \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3) \nPrincipal provider identifier;

    Section 7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to prioritize

    "source_version": "dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a", "title": "[PDF] CSBS Money
    Transmission Modernization Act", "extraction_state": "complete", "selected_passages":
    [{"unit_id": "p000028", "start": 0, "end": 2132, "page_number": 28, "section_label":
    null, "body_hash": "80c098d06593529d6d6335e3b8a4fe8e8db356a8c5d82eb34a2001d27d642973",
    "path": "03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md",
    "text": "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
    within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
    of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing of a petition by or against
    the licensee under the \nUnited States Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110,
    as amended or recodified from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization;
    \n(2) \nthe filing of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership,
    the commencement of any other judicial or administrative proceeding for its \ndissolution
    or reorganization, or the making of a general assignment for the benefit of its
    \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement of a proceeding to revoke or suspend
    its \nlicense in a state or country in which the licensee engages in business
    or is licensed. \n(b) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
    within three business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
    of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of the licensee
    or of a key individual \nor person in control of the licensee for a felony; or
    \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection
    7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports. \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file
    all reports required by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious
    activity reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and other
    federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely filing of \na
    complete and accurate report required under this [Section 7.05] with the appropriate
    federal \nagency is deemed compliant with the requirements of this [Section 7.05].
    \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a) \nLicensee shall maintain the following records,
    for determining its \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1)
    \na record of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2) \na
    general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability, capital,
    income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and bank reconciliation
    records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money transmission obligations;\n"}],

    "text": "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a licensee,

    under this [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner] may conduct

    take independent action authorized by this [Act] or by \na rule adopted or order

    4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee
